Remark
1. Remark 1.9\group harmonic-functions Source: han-lin-lecture-notes:page-0009 ↗ hanlin:thm-mean-value-max ↗ hanlin:thm-harmonic-mean-value ↗ hanlin:thm-mean-value-harmonic The preceding results give smoothness, the mean value property, and the maximum principle for harmonic functions. Thus the bounded-domain Dirichlet problem has at most one solution. On unbounded domains uniqueness can fail: on $\{ |x|>1\} $ the zero-boundary harmonic functions \[ u(x)=\log |x|\ (n=2),\qquad u(x)=|x|^{2-n}-1\ (n\ge 3) \] are nonzero, and $u(x)=x_n$ is a nonzero solution on the upper half-space.
